# Destination-specific contraction under a trip deletion

Use the existing MBTA development projection, all 512 requests, 48 simulated cancellations, five shuffled single-core repetitions and original route return type. Contract maximal forced paths for each destination. Ignore edges whose successors cannot reach the destination in the original timetable. Deletions cannot make these edges viable. If exactly one viable outgoing edge remains, its complete forced chain is necessary for every finite path. Summarize its trips by a 64-bit signature. A possible membership hit requires checking the actual trip before declaring a chain broken. Return every ride leg, including contracted ones. Compare with identical signature-based repair with contraction disabled, the exact wide-bitset lazy algorithm with and without pruning, the indexed CSA and all five original controls. Retain the prior decision rule of exact witnesses plus a 10% reduction in p95 and geometric-mean latency against every control, both gross and setup-amortized over these 48 batches. Resource model excludes graph construction common to all algorithms. Run this experiment on the existing development network only.
